2. Shortly, stated facts are that the petitioner in this Miscellaneous Case and the opposite party No. 2 made two General Diaries being General Diary No. 780 dated 15-11-96 and General Diary No. 88 dated 17-11-96 with the Mithapukur PS. The petitioner as first party made General Diary No. 783 dated 15-11-96 in the said police station against opposite party No. 2 and others stating that they were attempting to cut paddy from the waqf property of which the petitioner is the Mutawalli. It was stated in the General Diaries that a suit being other class suit No. 88 of 1992 for permanent injunction was filed in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Mithapukur Rangpur against the first party petitioner and his adhiars. The suit was decreed in favour of the opposite parties and then an appeal was taken by the defendant in the suit being other appeal No. 58 of 1994 and the appellate Court allowed the appeal and set aside the decree of the trial Court and consequently the suit for permanent injunction was dismissed. Against the Appellate decree the present opposite party preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division being Civil Revision No. 2260 of 1996. While issuing Rule on the revisional application this court made an order on 29-10-96 directing the parties to maintain status quo as to the possession of the suit land during the pendency of the Rule. It appears from the record that on the basis of the aforesaid general diaries, the officer in charge of the said police station submitted a report recommending for appointment of a receiver under section 145 CrPC stating that there was apprehension of breach of peace and the proceeding under section 145 CrPC was drawn by the learned Magistrate on 24-11-96 on the basis of the report submitted by the police pursuant to the two GD entries made by the parties and the officer in charge Mithapuur was appointed as receiver in respect of the disputed land and the case was fixed on 9-12-96 for filing written statements. The order for appointment of receiver was made after the order for maintaining status quo was passed by the High Court Division in the aforesaid civil revision and when the order was very much is force. Against the order drawing up proceeding and appointing receiver passed by the Magistrate a Criminal Revision being No. 95 of 1996 was taken to the learned Sessions Judge, Rangpur by the present petitioner and the learned Additional Sessions Judge after hearing the parties upheld the order of the learned Magistrate by the impugned order dated 15-6-98. It is against this order the present Rule was obtained by the petitioner. 

 3. Nahid Mahtab the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that when the civil Court and in this case the High Court Division being in session of the matter passed an order of maintaining status quo with regard to possession the learned Magistrate has no jurisdiction to draw proceeding under section 145 CrPC and consequently, the order dated 15-6-96 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge in Criminal Revision No. 95 of 1996 is without jurisdiction and the same is liable to be quashed and struck down. She further submits that the Rule in Civil Revision No. 2760 of 1996 has been discharged on 7-2-99. The learned Advocate has cited various decisions in support of her contention. Amongst the cited decisions the latest one is the case of Abul Bashar and another vs Hasanuddin Ahmed and others reported in 51 DLR (AD) 14 where it has been held that when the civil Court is already seized with the question of regulating possession of the land between the same parties the Magistrate acted without jurisdiction in initiating the proceeding under section 145 CrPC. Following the above principle we hold that the criminal court has no jurisdiction to draw up any proceeding under section 145 CrPC and the Magistrate's jurisdiction is completely ousted. Mr. Rasheduzzaman Basunia, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2, finds it difficult to make any submission supporting the order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. 

 4. We have heard the learned Advocate of both the parties and perused the paper, the impugned order and also the decision made by the Appellate Division in the above case and we are of the view that the impugned order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge on 15-6-98 in Criminal Revision No. 95 of 1996 upholding the order of the learned Magistrate drawing up proceeding under section 145 CrPC is without jurisdiction and the same is liable to be quashed and struck down.
